title: An Identity from Creation to Revocation
context: A new employee joins the team, needs occasional production access, and leaves the company six months later. You manage their identity in three decisions.

n1.text: The account must be created. What is the first step?

choices.text: Verify the requester's identity, validate the request, and assign minimum rights tied to their role
choices.why: Identity proofing and least privilege precede any rights assignment.

choices.text: Directly create an administrator account to avoid future requests
choices.why: This is a permanent, unjustified expansion of the attack surface.

choices.text: Share a colleague's account during onboarding

n2.text: They must apply an urgent production patch for two hours. How do you organize access?

choices.text: Grant just-in-time access, approved, automatically expiring, and logged
choices.why: JIT reduces the exposure window and leaves an audit trail of privilege elevation.

choices.text: Add their account to the permanent administrators group
choices.why: The privilege would remain active long after the work ends.

choices.text: Give them the service account password
choices.why: A service account is intended for an automated task, not human use.

n3.text: The employee leaves. Which revocation sequence is correct?

choices.text: Disable the account, revoke sessions and tokens, transfer assets, then retain logs
choices.why: Complete revocation covers account, sessions, tokens, and resource ownership.

choices.text: Wait until the end of the month to disable the account
choices.why: Unnecessary access remains an attack surface for the entire period.

choices.text: Delete audit logs to erase their traces
choices.why: On the contrary, logs are evidence of activity and must be retained.

n4.outcome: You applied a complete lifecycle: proofing, least privilege, JIT elevation, and verifiable revocation.

debrief: The quality of identity proofing underpins the entire lifecycle.
JIT limits the duration of elevated privileges and is paired with approval and logging.
Deprovisioning covers account, sessions, tokens, assets, and evidence retention.
